goal: python -m flywheel.audit <run_id> reads from the configured store and prints a human-readable chronological view by default, with --json switching to NDJSON and --follow enabling live tailing.

references: src/flywheel/workflow.py:44 and :631-766 -- existing argparse + main() pattern for python -m flywheel.workflow; mirror the parser construction, _cmd_* dispatch, and __main__ guard
src/flywheel/workflow.py:615-622 -- _add_common_db helper for --db argument resolution; reuse the same convention so audit picks up the same default store location
src/flywheel/audit.py -- stream() iterator the CLI consumes
constraints: Add a __main__.py to src/flywheel/audit/ OR convert audit.py to a package src/flywheel/audit/{__init__.py,__main__.py,_cli.py} -- the spec requires 'python -m flywheel.audit' to work. Choose the layout that keeps existing imports stable (the library was created in audit-stream-library as flywheel.audit module; if it is a single file, promote it to a package in this task and keep the public surface identical).

CLI flags: positional run_id (required); --db PATH (default: $FLYWHEEL_DB or ./flywheel.db, matching workflow.py convention); --json (NDJSON output, one record per line); --follow (live tail; exits when lifecycle reaches terminal status); --poll-interval FLOAT (default 0.25, only meaningful with --follow). No other flags -- the spec explicitly excludes --kind, --attempt, --summary as MVP non-goals.

Human-readable default output: one record per line. Format: '<iso-ts> seq=<n> attempt=<a> iter=<i> kind=<k> | <preview>'. <preview> is a short single-line summary: for EventRecord show event kind and a compact payload summary; for SdkMessageRecord show message_type and an elided preview of the body (~80 chars). Large payloads must NOT cause horizontal scrolling -- truncate the preview with an ellipsis and a hint like '... (use --json for full payload)'.

--json output: one JSON object per line (NDJSON). Each object has fields: ts, sequence, run_id, attempt_number, iteration_number (None for events), kind_or_message_type, payload (full, no truncation). ts is ISO-8601. The JSON output round-trips through json.loads without loss.
Unknown run_id: print 'no records for run_id <id>' to stderr and exit 0 (per spec error-handling table).
--follow against a terminal run: drains records and exits immediately. No polling latency in that path.

tests/test_audit.py: add CLI cases (use the keyword 'cli' so pytest -k cli selects them) covering (a) default mode prints all records in chronological order; (b) --json mode emits NDJSON; (c) unknown run_id prints the empty-state message and exits 0; (d) --follow exits when lifecycle reaches Status.DONE; (e) preview truncation hides multi-MB tool-result bodies in default mode but the full body is present in --json mode.

The CLI must work against SqliteStore -- the integration test opens a tmp sqlite db, writes a fixture run, then invokes 'python -m flywheel.audit <run_id> --db <path>' via subprocess and asserts the output.
Run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py file you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting verify.
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (e.g. 'feat:') before reporting verify.
non_goals: Do not add --kind, --attempt, --iteration, or --summary flags -- the spec explicitly defers these to a follow-up feature.
Do not add colorized output, pagers, or interactive controls -- plain stdout only.
Do not change the flywheel.audit library API; this task only adds the __main__ entry point and CLI plumbing.
edge_cases: Terminal width: the human-readable preview must remain on one line at typical terminal widths (80-120 cols). Do not call shutil.get_terminal_size() -- the preview budget is a fixed ~80-char tail so output is reproducible in tests and pipes.
Records with identical timestamps render in sequence order (the library already guarantees this; the CLI does not re-sort).
When --follow is interrupted by SIGINT/Ctrl-C, the CLI exits cleanly (0 or 130, your choice; document in --help) without a stack trace.

JSON serialization of non-JSON-native objects (datetimes, bytes): datetimes -> ISO-8601 strings; bytes -> base64 string. The library already persists payloads as JSON-compatible dicts so this rarely fires, but handle it defensively.
